stops.title: Ground-Level Hazard

supervisor.name: Dave
supervisor.dialogue: People have been walking around that spill all morning. Leave it, cleaning crew will get it later.

cordon_off.feedback: Great call. You controlled the risk instead of stepping around it. Alex moves to cordon off the spill area.

report_only.feedback: Reporting helps, but leaving an open slip hazard on a busy walkway puts people at risk. Alex moves to a safe observation position.

ignore.feedback: Walking past an active spill normalizes hazards and risks a serious slip. Alex follows Dave, accepting the unsafe condition.

stops.learning_objective: Never step around or normalize a slip hazard — secure the area immediately.

stops.title: Zone 02 | Blind-Corner Forklift Traffic

supervisor.name: Dave
supervisor.dialogue: Don't stop here, the forklift drivers know to watch for pedestrians. Just keep moving across.

hold_position.feedback: Spot on. You waited behind the hold line until the forklift cleared the junction, then crossed safely into the next zone.

proceed_carefully.feedback: Waving while walking is risky because tall cargo blocks the driver's sightlines. Alex moves cautiously.

walk_straight_through.feedback: Dangerous near-miss! Never assume a forklift operator sees you around blind corners. Alex follows Dave into the intersection.

stops.learning_objective: Always stop and make eye contact with forklift operators before crossing.

stops.title: Bent Rack Upright

supervisor.name: Dave
supervisor.dialogue: That upright has been bent for ages. It's held up fine, don't worry about it.

cordon_off.feedback: Great decision. Damaged rack columns can collapse without warning under heavy load. Alex cordons off the damaged bay.

report_only.feedback: Reporting is right, but the aisle stayed open under heavy pallet loads. Alex moves to a safe distance while reporting.

ignore.feedback: Familiar damage is still dangerous. Never ignore structural rack damage. Alex follows Dave past the structural risk.

stops.learning_objective: Always isolate and challenge structural damage, even if it has been there a long time.

stops.title: Charging Bay Warning Light

supervisor.name: Dave
supervisor.dialogue: Hold on — that charger is flashing an overheat fault and those boxes block airflow. Let's isolate it right now.

isolate_and_report.feedback: Spot on. You hit the emergency disconnect to prevent thermal runaway and a battery fire. Alex isolates the charging unit.

report_only.feedback: Reporting is good, but leaving an overheating charger powered risks an electrical fire. Alex moves clear to submit the ticket.

ignore.feedback: Flashing fault lights mean active danger. Leaving it running risks a major battery fire. Alex follows Dave past the fire risk.

stops.learning_objective: Treat early warning indicators as active emergencies — isolate power immediately.

stops.title: Clear Aisle Check

supervisor.name: Dave
supervisor.dialogue: Loading bay is in great shape — clear walkways and good sightlines. Our emergency response hub on the back wall is ready and unobstructed.

emergency_drill.feedback: Outstanding. You inspected the eyewash, AED, shower, fire extinguisher, and spill kit to ensure full emergency readiness. Alex concludes the safety patrol with distinction.

continue_on.feedback: The aisle is clear, but taking a moment to verify emergency equipment readiness saves lives. Alex completes the walk without an equipment check.

report_only.feedback: The zone is already compliant. Over-reporting clear areas creates unnecessary paperwork. Alex files the report.

stops.learning_objective: Confirm clear egress and verify that emergency response equipment is ready and accessible.

endOfSessionRules.feedback: Two warning signs went unaddressed. Ignoring both the fluid spill and the overheating charger led to an escalated workplace incident.
